newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Holzmann hit by CEO, cash worries.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Holzmann hit by CEO, cash worries.

text.p: Shares in German builder Philipp Holzmann AG fell sharply on Friday as talk of liquidity problems and unconfirmed reports that its chief executive faces dismissal added to existing nervousness about the stock.

Holzmann shares fell 20 marks to 330, a fall of nearly six percent, despite a denial earlier this week of a radio report that the company had liquidity problems and that its bank credit lines were at risk.
The company has yet to comment on a further report in Friday's mass circulation daily "Bild" newspaper that Mayer faced dismissal because of losses on a real estate project.

Analysts said the reports, while unsubstantiated, had taken their toll because of the continued uncertainty that has surrounded Holzmann since it shocked the market in 1995 with huge losses as a result of property write-downs.

"We've had these new rumours (of liquidity problems) a couple of months ago, but it just adds to the nervousness surrounding Holzmann when they resurface like this," Ingbert Faust, construction analyst at UBS in Frankfurt, said.

Holzmann on Wednesday denied a radio report that its banks had cut its credit lines, repeating a comment made with interim results in August that its financial projections were based on the assumption of sufficient liquidity in 1996 and 1997.

But a Holzmann spokesman on Friday said he could not immediately comment on a newspaper report that its chief executive Lothar Mayer may be facing dismissal because of losses on a real estate project.
A spokesman said an auditors' report on the losses was due to be presented to its supervisory board next Thursday and that he could not provide further information immediately.
Diversified industrial group Metallgesellschaft AG however swiftly denied speculation in the report that its management board chairman Kajo Neukirchen was being mooted to replace Mayer.
"The speculation is complete nonsense," a Metallgesellshaft spokesman said in response to enquiries.

Holzmann ran into financial problems in 1995, posting an unexpected loss of 443 million marks which forced it to omit its dividend payout. At the root of its problems were 458 million marks of write-downs on its property portfolio.
The group, which has suffered badly within the overall weakness in the German contracting sector, has said it expects an operating loss in 1996.
Analysts said that any change of chief executive at Holzmann might have implications for takeover plans that construction rival Hochtief AG has for the company.
Hochtief is currently attempting to overturn a ruling by the German cartel office that the takeover attempt cannot go ahead for competition reasons.
"Mayer was clearly a key figure opposing the takeover plans," one said.
